Drew Allar became one of the biggest talking points from Steelers training camp after a short video showed him missing a large practice net during a quarterback drill. The clip spread quickly across social media and triggered immediate debate among Steelers fans.The reaction centred on two things: the Aaron Rodgers comparison and the ongoing questions about Allar’s footwork in comparison to Will Howard.The throw came during a drill in which quarterbacks target pockets on a net. In the video, Drew Allar released the ball while looking away from the target, and the pass sailed well over the net. The post reads, “Can't say I've ever seen a quarterback just outright miss the net."Many fans gave mixed reactions: One fan said, “Allar is trying to spin like Rodgers.”The second fan added, “He tried doing a Aaron Rodgers-type throw with the footwork lol.”The third fan said, “One of the worst throws possible by Allar, still struggling with his footwork.”Another fan wrote, “Howard is him. Allar is trying to spin like Rodgers 👎”One more fan added, “Howard looks pretty smooth.”The same clip also drew attention to Will Howard’s performance. Howard hit his target cleanly during the drill and looked more controlled through the motion.Many fans praised his footwork, balance and release, and several comments said he appeared more comfortable and more accurate than Allar during the sequence. Because both quarterbacks are competing for developmental snaps behind Aaron Rodgers, the comparison quickly became part of the discussion around Pittsburgh’s young passers.The Pittsburgh Steelers selected the former Penn State quarterback with the 76th overall pick in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. The team drafted him for his size, arm strength and movement ability, not because he arrived as a polished NFL quarterback.Analyst Jim Wexell recently said Drew Allar still looks like a developmental passer, citing decision-making, touch, and footwork as the areas that need the most improvement. “Big, strong kid who can move, stand in the pocket, throw a great deep ball,” Wexell said during a recent training camp evaluation discussed by Steeler Nation. “Decision-making, finesse game, that’s really key. So, that’s going to have to come along a long way. ”That evaluation aligns with the main concern about Drew Allar’s game. His deep ball creates excitement, but NFL coaches will judge him on the routine throws, quicker decisions and cleaner mechanics that keep an offense on schedule. Reports from Steelers camp say head coach Mike McCarthy has emphasized footwork and mechanics through his quarterback development program, often called “QB School.”The coaching staff has focused on connecting each drop with the route concept and improving timing and balance.Aaron Rodgers remains the clear starter. The real discussion sits behind him. One throw will not decide whether Drew Allar or Will Howard becomes the Steelers’ future quarterback, but the clip brought fresh attention to the same developmental questions that McCarthy and the Steelers coaching staff are trying to answer during training camp.
Article Summary: Drew Allar became one of the biggest talking points from Steelers training camp after a short video showed him missing a large practice net during a quarterback drill. The clip spread quickly across social media and triggered immediate debate among Steelers fans. The reaction centred on the Aaron Rodgers comparison and the ongoing questions about Allar’s footwork in comparison to Will Howard.

Article Title: French trans basketball star Julie Tétart hopes to join WNBA following Sophie Cunningham’s controversial statement
Article Text:
Julie Tétart. Image via: Getty Images

Julie Tétart is eyeing a move to the WNBA

Julie Tétart dominated France's Ligue Féminine 2

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Julie Tétart's WNBA hopes gain spotlight amid Sophie Cunningham's comments

Julie Tétart, the French transgender basketball player who led her league in scoring and rebounding this past season, says she would accept a WNBA contract if one came her way. The comment surfaced as the league continues wrestling with a separate controversy involving Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, whose remarks opposing transgender participation in women's sports sparked protests, a suspension, and White House attention over the past several weeks.Tétart, who plays center for Monaco Basket Association in France's Ligue Féminine 2, told reporters she wasn't holding her breath but wouldn't turn down the opportunity either.Tétart's numbers from the 2025-26 LF2 season made the question worth asking. She averaged roughly 21 points and 20 rebounds per game, leading the league in both categories while playing at 6-foot-3. Despite that production, she was passed over for MVP, though she still collected Player of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year, and Domestic Player of the Year honors.Asked directly whether she'd consider trying out for a WNBA roster, Tétart didn't dismiss it. "I won't say no," she said. She followed that by noting the realistic obstacles facing a 34-year-old crossing over from a second-tier European league, pointing out that plenty of players in the WNBA are simply better equipped for that level. “But you have to be realistic: I'm old, and there are far better players than me!" Tétart told OutKick.Her dominance wasn't limited to a strong statistical average. During one March game, Tétart posted 21 points and 30 rebounds, setting a new league rebounding record and breaking her own previous mark. Such production is part of why French trans advocacy groups pushed back hard when she was left off the league's MVP ballot, a decision that also excluded fellow trans player Aurore Pautou despite her own strong season.Tétart addressed the possibility of a WNBA future carefully, calling it a longtime aspiration shared by any young female basketball player, but adding that circumstances outside the sport make it unlikely. She pointed to broader political conditions in the United States, without going into detail, as the sticking point rather than anything about the league itself.The timing put Tétart's comments squarely inside an ongoing WNBA debate. Cunningham, a seventh-year guard for the Fever, drew national attention after telling ESPN she supports keeping transgender athletes out of girls' and women's sports, framing her stance as protective rather than hostile. She stood by the comments the next day, telling reporters, "I said what I said. I think it's kind of common sense."Not everyone in the league agreed. Fever head coach Stephanie White pushed back on framing exclusion as any kind of solution, saying, "I don't ever believe that exclusion is an answer," while acknowledging she didn't consider herself well-versed in the underlying science. Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve went further, later telling reporters, "I come from a space of inclusion," and wearing a shirt reading "Trans Kids Belong" during a game against Indiana.Whether Tétart ever gets an actual roster offer remains an open question. For now, her answer stands on record, and the league's ongoing debate over transgender inclusion shows no sign of settling before training camps open.
Article Summary: Julie Tétart led France's Ligue Féminine 2 in scoring and rebounding this season. The 34-year-old center says she would accept a WNBA contract if one came her way. The comment surfaced as the league continues wrestling with a separate controversy involving Sophie Cunningham.

Article Title: 'You are a fool to live so openly, Mallya told Nirav before his arrest'
Article Text:
TOI correspondent from London

: Economic fugitive Vijay Mallya invited fellow billionaire Nirav Modi to his multi-million-pound townhouse overlooking Regent's Park where the pair discussed their respective exiles when the latter was living freely in London before his arrest, the final podcast of the "Diamond King", released Friday, claims.A source in the diamond trade who tipped off Telegraph about Nirav's location, leading to his arrest in March 2019, claims in Episode 4: "Mallya and Nirav were in contact... "Mallya told him he was a fool for living so openly and told him he was too exposed, but Nirav didn't listen.""It's possible Mallya's blueprint gave Nirav the confidence he didn't need to hide." But Nirav did not get bail and has been in a London jail for seven years.Despite an Interpol red notice, Nirav "would regularly stop for a cup of coffee at a cafe in Oxford Street where he would sit reading newspapers... where anyone could see him," the source said. However, he started taking precautions later. To avoid being seen in restaurants, he would pay private chefs £200 to £300 per hour to come to his apartment and cook, but they were never of Indian origin, and it was never the same chef twice, the podcast revealed."I don't think he was clever enough to come up with the (Punjab National Bank) scam himself," the source added. The podcast speculates that Nirav has submitted a second asylum case, which is why he has not gone back. Nirav's solicitor Anand Doobay, who Mallya also used, told TOI: "We are not commenting."

The pair discussed their respective exiles when the latter was living freely in London. A source in the diamond trade who tipped off Telegraph about Nirav's location, leading to his arrest in March 2019, claims in Episode 4: "Mallya and Nirav were in contact"

Wearing a swimsuit specially designed to accommodate her surgical scars, Sydney celebrated her body and the strength it had shown throughout years of treatment.Reflecting on her outlook, she said:Those words became a powerful reminder of the mindset that helped her face extraordinary challenges.Sydney's final TikTok upload arrived on July 29, when she happily shared that one of her favorite bands, Royal Otis, had dedicated a song to her during a concert. It was another example of how deeply her story had touched people far beyond social media.Although her family's latest update marks a difficult chapter, Sydney Towle's impact continues to extend well beyond her online following. Through honesty, resilience, and unwavering optimism, she transformed a deeply personal battle into a source of comfort and inspiration for countless others. As supporters continue to send messages of love and prayers, many are remembering not only the illness she faced but also the courage, hope, and positivity she chose to share every step of the way.

Article Title: Meet Betty Bromage: 97-year-old breaks her own Guinness World Record as oldest female wing walker after recovering from stroke
Article Text:
Meet Betty Bromage: 97-year-old breaks her own Guinness World Record as oldest female wing walker after recovering from stroke

Wing walk comes after recovering from stroke

'I'd just get bored otherwise'

Inspired by a message from her nursing days

Already planning a challenge for her 100th birthday

At an age when most people slow down, 97-year-old Betty Bromage has once again taken to the skies, this time to break her own Guinness World Record as the oldest female wing walker.The Cheltenham resident completed the daring challenge by being strapped to the top of an aircraft as it flew through the sky, raising money for the stroke unit at Cheltenham General Hospital, where she received treatment after suffering a stroke in 2025.The feat marks Bromage's sixth wing walk, with her first completed at the age of 87. She had previously set the Guinness World Record four years ago and has now reclaimed the title by surpassing her own achievement.Bromage suffered a stroke in 2025, which continues to affect her speech, but she said she was determined not to let it stop her from doing what she loves."They treated me so well," she told BCC, referring to the hospital staff who cared for her. "It affects my words, but the rest of me is fine."Her latest wing walk was organised to raise funds for the hospital's stroke unit as a way of thanking the medical team that helped her during her recovery.According to the hospital's charity, donations from the fundraiser will help purchase equipment that will benefit both patients and healthcare staff.Despite approaching her 100th birthday, Bromage says she has no plans to give up adventurous challenges."I'd just get bored of life otherwise," she said. "I can't drive, I can't see very well and I get a bit frustrated. So, I want to do the things I can do."Known for her fearless spirit, Bromage joked that the most difficult part of wing walking isn't flying through the air, it's climbing onto the aircraft."The only problem is getting up on the wing because I'm quite short. Once you're up there, no problem. The fairground is a lot worse," she said with a laugh.A former nurse, Bromage said her passion for fundraising was inspired by a quote she once saw displayed on a hospital wall."We pass through this world but once. Any good we can do, any kindness we can show, do it now. Do not defer or neglect it. You will not pass this way again," she recalled.She said those words have stayed with her throughout her life and continue to motivate her charitable work.Hospital charity representative Imogen Sims praised Bromage's extraordinary determination, saying staff were grateful for her support."To take on such a daring challenge to support our team is amazing," Sims said, adding that the funds raised would make a real difference for patients and staff alike.As for what's next, Bromage is already thinking ahead."I'll have to think of something when I'm 100," she said. "Something special."Her latest record-breaking wing walk has once again proven that age is no barrier to adventure, or to giving back to the community.
Article Summary: Betty Bromage, 97, breaks her own Guinness World Record as oldest female wing walker. Cheltenham resident completed the challenge by being strapped to the top of an aircraft as it flew through the sky. Bromage suffered a stroke in 2025, which continues to affect her speech, but she said she was determined not to let it stop her from doing what she loves.

Article Title: First total solar eclipse of 2026 falls on August 12: What makes it special, the best places to watch, and what you must never do
Article Text:
Representative image

Where the August 12 total solar eclipse will be visible

What makes this eclipse different from the 2024 one



How to watch the total solar eclipse live online



Solar eclipse safety: What not to do while watching



The Moon will slide fully across the Sun on the evening of August 12, dropping a narrow band of Europe into darkness for a little over a minute in some places and close to two in others. It is the first total solar eclipse anywhere on Earth since April 2024, and the first to cross the Iberian Peninsula in more than a century. Spain is the headline act here, simply because it is the only densely populated stretch of land the shadow touches.Totality begins over the Arctic, sweeps across eastern Greenland and western Iceland, clips a sliver of northeastern Portugal at Montesinho Natural Park, and then runs west to east across northern Spain. Everywhere else in Europe, and a chunk of North America, gets a partial bite out of the Sun instead.In Spain, León, Burgos, Valladolid, Santander, Bilbao, Zaragoza, Valencia and Palma all sit in the path of totality, with peak around 8:32-8:33 pm CEST. Madrid misses it by a hair at 99 percent obscuration. Iceland's western coast, including Reykjavík and Ísafjörður, sees totality earlier at 5:48 pm GMT, though Látrabjarg holds it longest.Elsewhere, Dublin gets 94 percent, Paris 92, London 91. North America does far worse. New York manages 9 percent, Washington DC just 4, and Chicago a rounding error at 0.1 percent. St John's in Newfoundland is the continent's best seat at 53 percent. India sees nothing, since the eclipse happens well past midnight IST.Two things. It coincides with lunar perigee, so the Moon appears slightly larger than usual and totality stretches longer than it otherwise would. It also lands on the Perseid meteor shower, which peaks the same night. Watch the eclipse at sunset, then wait for the sky to fill with meteors.ESA is streaming it free on YouTube and ESA Web TV from 19:30 to 20:45 CEST, hosted by space scientist Dame Dr Maggie Aderin. The main feed comes from the Observatorio Astrofísico de Javalambre in Teruel, where 1 minute 21 seconds of totality hits at 20:31 CEST, with additional feeds from León and Frómista as cloud insurance. ESA is also running a free public event at the Palacio de Exposiciones y Congresos in León, mostly in Spanish.Do not look at the Sun without certified eclipse glasses at any point outside totality. Sunglasses do not work. Binoculars and telescopes without solar filters are worse than nothing. The American Astronomical Society maintains a list of approved viewers. Shooting it? Your lens needs a solar filter too. The safest option costs nothing: a pinhole projector, or a kitchen colander held above the ground, which throws dozens of tiny crescent Suns onto the pavement.
Article Summary: The Moon will slide fully across the Sun on the evening of August 12, dropping a narrow band of Europe into darkness for a little over a minute in some places and close to two in others. It is the first total solar eclipse anywhere on Earth since April 2024, and the first to cross the Iberian Peninsula in more than a century.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit







El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

Article Title: IPL craze costs techie Rs 1.46 lakh in fake RCB vs CSK ticket scam
Article Text:

RCB register their second win

NEW DELHI: IPL comes and the demand for tickets and passes go soaring up by the fans. The desperation to get inside the stadium to watch their favourite teams in action in the IPL go high and high. When the tickets get sold out, the demand gets too hig, and the cricket fans even ask for tickets in black. But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. In reply, CSK faltered under scoreboard pressure, with Sarfaraz Khan’s 50 off 24 balls and Prashant Veer’s 43 the lone acts of resistance amid a string of failures from the top order.Bhuvneshwar was at his disciplined best and even crossed the 200-mark in terms of wickets in IPL, with others also chipping in as CSK were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) beat Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday. Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal put on a marauding batting show to lift RCB to a daunting 250/3. RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.

Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: Fake IDs, dual lives, and a dramatic escape: The 28-year saga of killer Rajinder Bairagi
Article Text:
Over two decades, Bairagi built a quiet, respectable life, marrying an auxiliary nur-se at the local govt hospital and raising two children.

Probe Into 2 Cold Cases Leads Police To Man Who Killed Haryana Cop





NEW DELHI: Ending a nearly three-decade game of hide-and-seek, the Delhi Police crime branch has captured Rajinder Bairagi, a fugitive wanted for the 1998 murder of Haryana Police personnel Jai Bhagwan. Police also claimed to have cracked two attempted murder cases that had remained unsolved since 1997.A former kabaddi player-turned-criminal, Bairagi’s journey into crime began decades earlier in Haryana’s Sonipat, where his involvement in competitive sports brought him into contact with local criminal networks, according to special CP (crime) HGS Dhaliwal.That path culminated in the deadly May 1998 wedding shooting in Saiyan Khera village, where Bairagi and five associates fired indiscriminately following a heated dispute, leaving Jai Bhagwan dead and another individual critically wounded.Though arrested shortly after, Bairagi staged a dramatic breakout on Feb 14, 1999, escaping UP Police custody at Gannaur railway station while fully restrained in handcuffs during a court transit from Ghaziabad Jail. From there, he vanished.For 28 years, Bairagi managed to evade justice. He initially spent a year teaching physical education in Mumbai’s Colaba before reinventing himself as “Rajender Singh Yadav” in Mungaoli, in Madhya Pradesh’s Ashok Nagar district.Over two decades, Bairagi built a quiet, respectable life, marrying an auxiliary nurse at the local govt hospital and raising two children. He meticulously constructed a fresh identity, seamlessly integrating into the local fabric, securing complete sets of forged official identity documents, including a domicile certificate, driving licence, voter ID, PAN card and local credentials.Alongside his property business, he operated a small private clinic, where residents knew him casually as “Dr Jhatka”. To the outside world, he was simply a family man living alongside his wife and their two children, completely detached from his violent history.His elaborate cover finally unravelled when a team led by DCP Chander Singh started probing two attempted murder cases which had gone cold. One of the cases, dating back to June 1997, was registered at Janakpuri police station, and involved a brutal knife attack in Uttam Nagar, for which Bairagi was declared a proclaimed offender by Rohini courts in 2008.As the team dug deeper into his background, they uncovered the high-profile nature of his past crimes. Tracking down a fugitive so deeply embedded in a fake persona required a combination of traditional field operations and modern forensics. Cops developed ground intelligence and used technical surveillance and digital footprint analysis. Together, these confirmed his location, verified his daily routine and mapped his exact movements in MP.With the target confirmed, a police team, led by inspector Sanjay Kaushik and comprising SI Deepak Kumar and others, conducted a raid in Mungaoli and nabbed Bairagi.
Article Summary: Rajinder Bairagi is a fugitive wanted for the 1998 murder of Haryana Police personnel Jai Bhagwan. Police also claimed to have cracked two attempted murder cases that had remained unsolved since 1997. A former kabaddi player-turned- criminal, his journey into crime began decades earlier. He meticulously constructed a fresh identity, seamlessly integrating into the local fabric.

Article Title: 'Don't want another Kejriwal': CJP faces internal dissent as 2 youth stage protest outside Abhijeet Dipke's home
Article Text:
2 youths demonstrated in front of Abhijeet Dipke's residence, highlighting their concerns about grassroots volunteers being sidelined





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: A fresh rift appears to have emerged within the Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ), with two youth claiming to be part of last month's Delhi agitation staging a protest outside founder Abhijeet Dipke's residence in Maharashtra on Thursday.Alleging that grassroots volunteers were excluded from key organisational discussions, one of them launched an indefinite fast, saying, "We don't want another Kejriwal."The protest took place outside Dipke's residence in the Waluj MIDC area, where the CJP's core team has been holding meetings since Wednesday to discuss the movement's future course.The two protesters, who identified themselves as Manish Brahmabhatt and Rahul Pandya from Ahmedabad, said they had actively participated in the student-led agitation at Delhi's Jantar Mantar last month but were not invited to the ongoing strategy meeting."When the CJP's agitation began, it was faceless. I, along with many other volunteers, contributed to the agitation at Jantar Mantar (in New Delhi). I came here and tried to meet the CJP team. But nobody met me here. I was not even called for the meeting," Brahmabhatt said.Questioning the way decisions were being taken, he said, "Cousins and friends are sitting together, and they cannot decide the way ahead of the protest as this agitation was of the entire country."Demanding a more democratic structure within the organisation, Brahmabhatt said those who worked on the movement should have been given an opportunity to share their views."There should be democracy in the organisation, and people who have worked in the agitation should have been called to put forth their suggestions,"he said.Announcing an indefinite fast outside Dipke's residence, Brahmabhatt added, "We don't want another Kejriwal. I am sitting on an indefinite fast here itself now."The CJP-led protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar last month, centred around the alleged NEET paper leak and other examination irregularities, triggered a nationwide political debate and eventually led to the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.The party's core leadership is currently meeting in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar to chart its next course.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Youths stage protest outside founder Abhijeet Dipke's residence in Maharashtra. Alleged that grassroots volunteers were excluded from key organisational discussions. One of them launched an indefinite fast, saying, "We don't want another Kejriwal"

Article Title: Marathi literary luminary Shrinivas Kulkarni passes away at 92
Article Text:
Writer, editor Shrinivas Kulkarni

Kolhapur

:





Renowned Marathi prose writer and essayist Shrinivas Vinayak Kulkarni, popularly known as ‘Shrivi’, passed away at Karad on Thursday following a prolonged illness. He was 92.Kulkarni, considered one of the most distinctive voices in Marathi prose, is survived by his wife, two sons, daughters-in-law and grandchildren. His last rites were performed in Karad on Thursday evening in the presence of family members and members of the literary fraternity.Widely acclaimed for his landmark work ‘Doh’, Kulkarni brought to life the landscape, people and memories of Audumbar, his village in Sangli district, on the banks of Krishna river.Paying tribute to his literary brilliance, noted writer Venkatesh Madgulkar had once remarked: “Had ‘Balkavi’ (the pen name of nature poet Tryambak Bapu Thombre) tried to write prose, then it would have been like Shrinivas Kulkarni’s work.”Born on Nov 20, 1936, in Audumbar, Kulkarni completed his primary education in the village and later studied at Ankalkhop and Sangli. After working briefly as a signboard painter and in a glass factory, he joined Mouj publication and went on to edit the influential literary magazine for several years, nurturing generations of Marathi writers.Though he began his literary journey as a poet, writing his first poem while studying in Class IV, Kulkarni eventually found his true calling in prose.His first essay, ‘Manatlya Unhat’, was published in ‘Satyakatha’ in 1960, marking the beginning of a celebrated writing career.His major prose collections include ‘Doh’ (1965), ‘Sonyacha Pimpal’ (1975), ‘Panyache Pankh’ (1987) and ‘Kordi Bhiksha’ (2000), all of which were first published in ‘Satyakatha’ and ‘Mouj’ before being compiled into books.Earlier this year, Maharashtra govt announced the Vinda Karandikar Lifetime Achievement Award for Kulkarni.Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis condoled his death, stating: “With his demise, we have lost a steadfast, sensitive figure from the Marathi literary world. Through ‘Mouj’, he provided a platform to numerous emerging writers, he gave a new direction to the Marathi literary world. With his passing, we have lost a dedicated, inspirational figure who served Marathi literature with steadfastness.”Former chief minister Prithviraj Chavan said, “In passing of Shrinivas Kulkarni, Maharashtra has lost someone who dedicated for making Marathi literature rich. As a resident of Karad town, we were very proud to have Kulkarni as a resident of the town.”
